developer_and_jurisdiction: The getfireshot.com footer reads '© 2008 — 2026 TruePage Solutions LTDA.' On Firefox AMO the developer is listed as Evgeny Suslikov. The license agreement names the licensor as 'GETFIRESHOT.COM and its licensors, if any', and its only contact is contacts@getfireshot.com. No address or country appears on getfireshot.com, license.php, privacy.php or extension-policy.php. A web search found no Brazilian (CNPJ) or other registry record for 'TruePage Solutions LTDA'. The 'LTDA' suffix only hints at a Brazilian or Portuguese-style entity, and that is unverified. Section 11 of the license (SLA) says it 'shall be governed by the internal laws of the State of California'. It also names the 'exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the state courts sitting in San Francisco County, California, or the federal courts in California' (https://getfireshot.com/license.php). The Chrome Web Store listing says 'This developer has not identified itself as a trader', so EU consumer rights do not apply to contracts with it. That listing gives no developer name or address, only getfireshot.com and contacts@getfireshot.com.
license: Proprietary freemium. Lite is free, and 'Advertisements' appears as a row in the features comparison. Pro is paid. AMO lists the license as 'Custom License'. It is not open source. Pricing on https://getfireshot.com/buy.php as of 2026-11-07: 'FireShot Pro – Yearly' at $39.95/year, labeled 'Save 60%' ('Only $3.33 per month'), or 'FireShot Pro – Lifetime License' at $99.95 one-time. buy.php says the Lifetime plan gives 'Unlimited usage on two devices' (multiple browsers or profiles, personal use only). The SLA instead says 'up to two desktop (home and work) and two laptops.' A money-back guarantee is not stated on buy.php, using.php or privacy.php. Only user forum posts mention one, and they conflict (7 days vs 30 days), so it is unverified. Payment provider: FastSpring, listed as a service provider in the privacy policy. Pro trial: 10 days, after which it reverts to the free version (https://getfireshot.com/using.php). Older third-party listings show a $39.95 one-time lifetime price, which suggests the pricing has changed; those listings were not re-fetched.
platforms: A browser extension, not a standalone desktop capture app. Chrome Web Store: v2.1.4.18, updated May 24, 2026, 3,000,000 users, 4.9 from 53K ratings. Firefox AMO: v1.12.18, last updated Jun 5, 2023, 183,707 users. Chromium browsers such as Edge and Opera can install from the Chrome Web Store. Older docs list other browsers (Pale Moon, SeaMonkey, IE, Thunderbird); these were not re-verified in this pass. The advanced features (editing, printing, capturing all tabs in one click, and others) need the Windows helper installed via https://getfireshot.com/enable-advanced.php. That page says 'the advanced features are not available on other platforms at the moment'. AMO lists the 'Exchange messages with programs other than Firefox' permission, which is native messaging. It captures web page content and the browser window only.
price: Lite: free, with ads. Pro: $39.95/year (labeled 'Save 60%') or $99.95 one-time lifetime, per buy.php on 2026-11-07. Pro trial: 10 days.
privacy_network: The extension policy (https://getfireshot.com/extension-policy.php, undated) says settings are stored locally, 'This data is not sent outside of the user's PC', and the extension 'does not send out any personal information'. It does not mention analytics. The Chrome Web Store disclosure says the developer will not collect or use user data. However, the AMO privacy policy (https://addons.mozilla.org/en/firefox/addon/fireshot/privacy/, fetched directly) says: 'FireShot uses Google Analytics to collect anonymized usage data related to extension performance and reliability'. It adds that this is 'opted in by default, and can be opted out in the extension's options.' Tabs that open on start or update go to getfireshot.com and fall under the website privacy policy. That policy (https://getfireshot.com/privacy.php, 'Updated: October 10, 2019') names Google Analytics and Adwords (cookies), plus FastSpring and ZenDesk as service providers. Optional uploads: EasyCaptures, Flickr, Picasa, ImageShack, Twitter, and custom FTP or HTTP servers.

Some code is derived from other projects: Lightscreen (GPLv2), a few lines from KSnapshot (LGPL), and Qt-Color-Widgets (LGPL/GPL). platforms: Windows, macOS and Linux. flameshot.org says "64-bit only" for each platform. The README calls GNOME and Plasma Wayland support experimental; flameshot.org itself does not mention Wayland. price: Free and open source. Source: https://flameshot.org/
developer_and_jurisdiction: A community open-source project in the flameshot-org GitHub organization; maintainer borgmanJeremy publishes releases. The site names no company, imprint or legal address, so the jurisdiction is unknown. privacy_network: The README privacy section says the program "will not transfer any information to other networked systems" unless "specifically requested by the user or the person installing or operating it." Two caveats come from the source. First, upstream builds check for updates by default: confighandler.cpp sets checkForUpdates to true unless DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECKER is defined, and that CMake option defaults to OFF. Second, Imgur upload is off by default: CMakeLists.txt has option(ENABLE_IMGUR ... OFF), and OMG! Ubuntu reported in Aug 2025 that 13.0 disabled it, citing the risk of accidentally uploading sensitive data. I could not open the openSUSE patch (HTTP 403), so the claim that openSUSE removes the update check is unverified.

v13.2.0 (27 Oct) called #4169 'an improvement (but not final fix)'. v14.0.0 then switched to asking which monitor to capture instead of drawing one overlay across all monitors, noting this helps with mixed scaling, and added fractional-scaling and HiDPI region fixes. v15 fixed pin size on scaled Windows screens and capture when logical min/max coordinates are not zero (#4735)

Subcommands gui, screen, full, launcher and config, with options for path, delay, clipboard, region, raw, upload, pin and more. The docs say Windows users must use flameshot-cli. v15 fixed and improved the Windows CLI (#4881, #4888)
GPLv3+ (README)

notable_facts.claim: v15.0.0 shipped 2026-11-07, after v15.0.rc1 on 2026-09-19. It added an arrow style selector (#4769), hex GUI colors, keyboard controls for the monitor selector, mouse-wheel stepping for the circle counter, and an X11 fallback when the portal is unavailable. It enabled Control Flow Guard for MSVC builds (#4967), fixed the Windows CLI (#4881, #4888), fixed pin size on scaled Windows screens (#4907), and fixed capture with non-zero logical coordinates (#4735).

CORRECTION: v14.0.0 was released on 19 Jun 2026, after rc1 and rc3, so the sequence was 13.x, then v14, then v15. v14 added the monitor-selection prompt, Capture Active Monitor (X11 and Windows; not Wayland), a Windows global screenshot hotkey and portable config mode.
CORRECTION: Capture Active Monitor came in v14.0.0, not v13.3. v13.3.0 was a macOS hotfix plus memory-leak fixes.
CORRECTION: #799 ('Capture single window') was closed as completed in Sep 2020 and never formally marked a duplicate of #5. The live tracking issue for window selection is #5, which is still open.

CORRECTION: The GIF request #172 is still open with an Enhancement label, not declined. #2201 (screen recording) was closed as a duplicate of #172, with maintainers calling recording out of scope or plugin-only.

CORRECTION: OCR PR #3074 is still open and unmerged, not formally declined. A maintainer stated in review that OCR is out of scope and belongs in a plugin, and called this a unanimous decision by the devs.

CORRECTION: The OMG! Ubuntu article says Imgur was disabled in 13.0 because of accidental-upload risk. It names no compile flag and gives no plugin plan. The ENABLE_IMGUR CMake option, default OFF, is confirmed in CMakeLists.txt.
CORRECTION: Frozen-screen capture changed from partial to unknown, because no cited source documents it.

CORRECTION: The openSUSE patch URL returned HTTP 403, so the claim that openSUSE removes the update check is unverified. That upstream defaults checkForUpdates to true is verified in confighandler.cpp, along with DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECKER defaulting to OFF in CMakeLists.txt.
The Wayland 'experimental' label comes from the README, not flameshot.org. The '64-bit only' statement comes from flameshot.org.

The README still states that on Windows the Print Screen global shortcut is fixed and cannot be changed, and that the config is at C:\Users\{YOURNAME}\AppData\Roaming\flameshot\flameshot.ini. v14 release notes mention a Windows global screenshot hotkey, so the README may be out of date on this point.

Scope stays at 'screenshot and annotation'. Maintainers called OCR (#3074) and screen recording (#2201) out of scope or plugin-only. Window selection (#5) and scrolling capture (#1130) remain open and unimplemented.
No company, imprint or legal jurisdiction is identified. The site footer credits 'Flameshot contributors', and no corporate entity was found. Jurisdiction is unknown, not verified as absent.

license: GPL-3.0. GitHub repo license metadata says GPL-3.0, and the FAQ says "Greenshot is free in terms of the GNU General Public License (GPL)". The Mac App Store build is a separate paid app.
platforms: Windows: the FAQ says "Greenshot 1.3 is built for the Microsoft .NET Framework 4.7.2 and needs version 4.7.2 or newer to run." An FAQ entry that says "Greenshot no longer supports Windows versions before Windows 10" is marked obsolete and points to the .NET requirements entry instead. macOS: a separate paid Mac App Store app, version 1.2.19, last updated June 29, 2020, requiring macOS 10.12 or later. App Store reviews say its editor has far fewer tools than the Windows version.
price: Windows: free. macOS: USD 1.99 on the Mac App Store, seller Thomas Braun (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/greenshot/id1103915944?mt=12, checked 2026-11-07).
latest_version: Stable: 1.3.328, the newest GitHub release that is not a pre-release and the one the API returns as "latest". Its notes call it the 11th stable release of the 1.3 series and say 1.3.324 to 1.3.327 were intermediate builds, even though the body opens with "Pre-release of Greenshot 1.3.328." Development: 1.4.459-gd17fcce94b, a continuous-build pre-release.
developer_and_jurisdiction: The website imprint (https://getgreenshot.org/impressum/) says Greenshot and getgreenshot.org are run by Thomas Braun, Jens Klingen and Robin Krom. Jens Klingen is the representative and the person responsible for content, at Markgrafenstr. 4, 91207 Lauf, Germany. The imprint is headed "Information in accordance with §5 TMG (Telemedia Act - Germany)". It names the content-responsible person "according to § 55 paragraph 2 RStV (Interstate Broadcasting Treaty - Germany)". It also says "The contents and works on these websites prepared by the operator of the websites shall be subject to German copyright law." It gives no company, commercial register entry or VAT ID, so it appears to be run by individuals rather than a registered firm. The privacy policy (https://getgreenshot.org/privacy-policy/) names only "the Greenshot development team", with no legal entity. It does not mention GDPR/DSGVO and has no governing-law clause. The software is licensed under GPL-3.0, not a German-law EULA. Supported wording: the website is operated from Germany by individuals and carries a German-law imprint (TMG/RStV), and the site's own content is stated to be subject to German copyright law. Not supported by any source: that the software is governed by German law, or that German law constrains its features. Mac App Store seller: Thomas Braun.
privacy_network: The privacy policy says the Windows app sends no data to Greenshot's or other servers unless the user starts or configures a transfer, such as an upload plugin, with one exception: the update check. The update check is on by default, fetches a file from the website, and lets GitHub and Cloudflare see the requesting IP address. The policy says the Mac app sends no data. Telemetry is not mentioned. The website uses Google Analytics (configured, the policy says, to store only anonymized IP addresses), Google AdSense ads with third-party cookies, Cloudflare CDN, Google Fonts and GitHub Pages hosting. The Mac App Store listing has no privacy label ("No Details Provided"). Upload plugins named in the 1.3.323 notes: Imgur, Box, Dropbox, Flickr, Confluence and Jira. Recent security fixes: 1.3.323 (2026-10-08) fixed TLS certificate validation that was disabled process-wide, which exposed OAuth tokens and plugin uploads to man-in-the-middle attacks (GHSA-q4w7-9m8v-53fm). 1.3.328 (2026-10-19) fixed Greenshot sending the user's Windows credentials to any server it requested content from, so a malicious image URL could trigger an automatic NTLM authentication exchange (GHSA-gjcr-pccx-w2vg).

features.feature: Works fully offline / no telemetry by default
features.note: No data is sent without user action except the update check, which is on by default and exposes the IP address to GitHub and Cloudflare. The policy does not mention telemetry.

Stable: issue #542 'HDR correction?' is open (since 2024-06-04). The 1.4 dev branch merged HDR work on 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-04 (PR #1675 JPEG XR HDR output, #1688 whole-capture HDR image, #1689 HDR parts joining). Not in a stable release.

In the 1.4 dev branch, PR #1628 (merged 2026-10-29) fixes an editor error when the editor opens on a monitor with another DPI, and PR #1451 (merged 2026-11-05) sizes editor icons for the display. This suggests mixed-DPI issues in stable. No explicit support statement.
FAQ: 'Yes, a few are implemented'. Run the executable with a help parameter to list them.
GPL-3.0, github.com/greenshot/greenshot, about 5.2k stars (5,243 on 2026-11-07). The Mac App Store build is a separate paid app.

notable_facts.claim: Maintenance is active. The repo was last pushed 2026-11-07T00:09Z. Non-pre-release 1.3.x builds came out on 2026-01-07 (1.3.311 and 1.3.312), 2026-03-20, 2026-10-08 and 2026-10-19. Four 1.4 pre-release builds came out between 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-06.
The 1.3.323 release notes say that while working on Greenshot 1.4, the team selectively backported improvements to stabilize 1.3. Every 1.4 release so far is marked pre-release.

1.3.328 (2026-10-19) fixed Greenshot sending the user's Windows credentials to any server it requested content from, so a malicious image URL could trigger NTLM authentication (GHSA-gjcr-pccx-w2vg). It also code-signed all shipped executables and DLLs so Windows Smart App Control no longer blocks them (PR #1505).

1.3.323 (2026-10-08) fixed TLS certificate validation that was disabled process-wide, exposing OAuth tokens and plugin uploads (Imgur, Box, Dropbox, Flickr, Confluence, Jira) to man-in-the-middle attacks. It also fixed a CF_DIBV5 clipboard out-of-bounds read (GHSA-4674-75g5-79mx), an SVG SSRF (GHSA-mmr7-mfv6-wp78), and vulnerable Inno Setup and log4net dependencies.

The website imprint cites §5 TMG and §55 para. 2 RStV and gives Jens Klingen, Markgrafenstr. 4, 91207 Lauf, Germany, as representative and responsible for content. It names no company, register or VAT ID, and it states that the site's content 'shall be subject to German copyright law'. This concerns the website, not the GPL-licensed software.

The privacy policy names only 'the Greenshot development team' (no legal entity), has no governing-law clause and does not mention GDPR. The website uses Google Analytics (anonymized IPs), Google AdSense, Cloudflare and Google Fonts.
The Mac App Store version (1.2.19, $1.99, seller Thomas Braun) was last updated 2020-06-29, requires macOS 10.12+, and has no privacy label. Reviews say its editor lacks many Windows features.

Annotations in .greenshot/.gst files from 1.2 to 1.4 are saved with .NET BinaryFormatter. PR #1506 (open, experimental) adds a zip+JSON document format that can read old files without BinaryFormatter.

Many 1.4 PRs by maintainer Robin Krom (Lakritzator) in Oct-Nov 2026 (for example #1454, #1506, #1537, #1546, #1628, #1641, #1675) carry a 'claude-projects-attribution' HTML comment and a 'Generated with Claude Code' footer in their body. This shows AI-assisted development.
Video recording (#203, since 2020), screen pinning (#711) and scrolling capture (#624) are open requests, and none is in a stable release.
CORRECTION: PR #1451 (DPI-sized editor icons) was merged on 2026-11-05, not in October 2026 as the original research said.

CORRECTION: The FAQ entry 'no longer supports Windows versions before Windows 10' is marked obsolete and redirects to the .NET Framework 4.7.2 requirement. Treat .NET 4.7.2+ as the stated requirement, not a Windows 10 minimum.
CORRECTION: The speech bubble and counter tools date to Greenshot 1.2 (December 2014), not 1.2.9. The BetaNews source returned 403 and was replaced with the official 1.2 announcement.

CORRECTION: The original 'Frozen-screen' note implied live selection replaces frozen selection. PR #1537 actually adds an option, 'Freeze the screen while selecting', which is on by default, so frozen selection remains the default.
CORRECTION: The 'BinaryFormatter' fact was scoped only to the 1.4 dev branch. PR #1506 says .greenshot/.gst files from versions 1.2 to 1.4 all use BinaryFormatter.
CORRECTION (minor): 1.3.311 was also a non-pre-release build on 2026-01-07, alongside 1.3.312.
